method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Diagnosis needs all three:** glucose over 11 mmol/L; venous pH under 7.3 or bicarbonate under 18 mmol/L; ketonaemia of 3 mmol/L or more or ketonuria of 2+ or more.
claims.source_text: The biochemical criteria for diagnosis of DKA are all three of Serum glucose >11 mmol/L Venous pH <7.3 or bicarbonate <18 mmol/L Ketonaemia (ketones ≥3 mmol/L) or ketonuria (ketones ≥2+ on urinalysis)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Severity by the worse of venous pH and bicarbonate:** mild pH under 7.3 / bicarbonate under 18 · moderate under 7.2 / under 10 · severe under 7.1 / under 5.
claims.source_text: Assessed based on the more severe of these parameters: Venous pH Bicarbonate (mmol/L) Mild <7.3 <18 Moderate <7.2 <10 Severe <7.1 <5
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Euglycaemic ketoacidosis** (BGL under 14 mmol/L with acidosis and ketonaemia) can follow starvation, low-carbohydrate diets or off-label SGLT2 inhibitor use. **Consult a specialist early.**
claims.source_text: Euglycaemic ketoacidosis is a clinical syndrome occurring both in type 1 and type 2 diabetes mellitus characterized by BGL <14 mmol/L Metabolic acidosis (arterial pH <7.3, serum bicarbonate <18 mmol/L) Ketonaemia ≥3 mmol/L … Can be caused by starvation, a low carbohydrate diet or off-label use of SLGT2-inhibitors. Consult a specialist early regarding management
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Clinical estimates of dehydration are often inaccurate in DKA**, as acidosis exaggerates peripheral shutdown. Weigh the child.
claims.source_text: Children with DKA will be dehydrated, however clinical estimates of volume depletion based on physical exam are often inaccurate, as acidosis may exacerbate peripheral shutdown … Weigh child, compare with recent weight if available
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Initial bloods (insert the IV cannula at the same time):** glucose, venous gas, point-of-care ketones, UEC, calcium, magnesium, phosphate, FBE.
claims.source_text: Bloods - insert IV cannula when taking bloods Serum glucose level Venous blood gas Point of care blood ketones UEC, calcium, magnesium, phosphate FBE
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Until DKA resolves:** BGL and bedside ketones hourly; VBG, UEC, Ca, Mg and PO4 at 2 hours and 2–4-hourly thereafter.
claims.source_text: Hourly: BGL, bedside ketone testing At 2 hours and 2-4 hourly thereafter: VBG, UEC, Ca, Mg, PO4
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Nurse head up; nil by mouth until alert** (ice to suck is fine). Cardiac monitoring for potassium-related ECG changes. Consider antibiotics for febrile children with signs of infection.
claims.source_text: Nurse head up … Keep nil by mouth until child is alert, and preferably until acidosis resolves Children can be given ice to suck on for comfort … Cardiac monitoring for assessment of ECG changes related to potassium levels … Consider antibiotics for febrile children with signs of infection
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Intubation is rarely needed** and maintaining respiratory compensation afterwards is complex — **get critical care advice before intubating.**
claims.source_text: It is rare for children with DKA to require intubation and ventilation. Maintaining respiratory compensation after intubation can be complex and early critical care advice prior to embarking on intubation is advised
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most children can start on the 'mild' or 'moderate' fluid rate**, since clinical estimates of deficit are unreliable.
claims.source_text: Clinical estimates of fluid deficits are subjective and often inaccurate, thus most children can initially be safely commenced on the 'mild' or 'moderate' fluid rate
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tachycardic with delayed central capillary refill:** a 10 mL/kg bolus of 0.9% sodium chloride over 30 minutes, then reassess.
claims.source_text: A bolus of 10 mL/kg 0.9% sodium chloride can be given over 30 minutes to children who are tachycardic with delayed central capillary refill
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Rehydrate with 0.9% sodium chloride**, continued for at least the first 6 hours. The tabulated rates are maintenance plus deficit over 48 hours; factor in prior resuscitation, especially over 20 mL/kg.
claims.source_text: Commence rehydration with 0.9% sodium chloride … IV fluids containing 0.9% sodium chloride should be continued for at least the first 6 hours … The fluid rates below represent maintenance plus replacement of hydration deficit over a 48-hour period. Prior fluid resuscitation should be factored into fluid replacement, especially if the child has received >20 mL/kg
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Once BGL is 15 mmol/L or less, change to 0.9% sodium chloride with 5% glucose** (plus potassium chloride, maximum 60 mmol/L). **Aim for BGL 5–10 mmol/L.**
claims.source_text: Once BGL is ≤15 mmol/L change fluids to 0.9% sodium chloride with 5% glucose and potassium chloride (maximum 60 mmol/L) as required … Aim to keep the BGL between 5-10 mmol/L
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If BGL falls below 5, or falls faster than 5 mmol/L/hour between 5 and 15 while still acidotic, increase glucose to 10%.** Reduce insulin only if BGL keeps falling on 10% glucose.
claims.source_text: If BGL falls below 5 mmol/L or is falling rapidly (>5 mmol/L/hour) in the range between 5-15 mmol/L and the child remains acidotic, increase the glucose content to 10% … Insulin infusion rate should only be decreased if BGL continues to fall despite glucose concentration of 10%
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Correct the sodium:** measured Na + 0.4 × (glucose − 5.5). Discuss corrected Na under 125 or over 150 mmol/L with a senior doctor early. **Any hypotonic fluid must be at least 0.45% sodium chloride.**
claims.source_text: Corrected sodium = measured sodium + 0.4 x (glucose – 5.5) mmol/L … Extremes of corrected sodium (Na <125 mmol/L or Na >150 mmol/L) should be discussed with a senior doctor early … If a hypotonic solution is required, minimum sodium chloride content should be 0.45%
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stop IV fluids once pH and bicarbonate have normalised and oral intake is tolerated.**
claims.source_text: IV fluids can be ceased once pH and bicarbonate have normalised … and the child is able to tolerate oral intake (this usually coincides with insulin being changed to subcutaneous injections)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Add 40 mmol/L potassium chloride if serum K is 5.5 mmol/L or less and the child is passing urine**, up to 60 mmol/L to keep K normal. **No potassium if anuric or K over 5.5.**
claims.source_text: Use fluid containing 40 mmol/L potassium chloride if the serum potassium ≤5.5 mmol/L and the child is passing urine … If anuric or serum potassium >5.5 mmol/L, do not use potassium containing fluids until this has improved … Start potassium chloride at a concentration of 40 mmol/L, increasing to a maximum 60 mmol/L if required to maintain serum potassium in the normal range
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **If K is under 3.0 mmol/L, replace potassium before starting insulin.** Recheck K within one hour of starting insulin, then two- to four-hourly.
claims.source_text: If the child is hypokalaemic (K+ <3.0 mmol/L) replace potassium prior to commencement of insulin … Once insulin is commenced, a repeat serum potassium should be measured within one hour and two- to four-hourly thereafter
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Use premixed potassium bags where possible; never add potassium chloride to a bag already hanging.**
claims.source_text: Use pre-mixed fluid bags containing potassium where possible … Do not add potassium chloride to a bag that is already hanging
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Phosphate below 0.32 mmol/L:** consider IV replacement per local protocol, and monitor calcium closely if given.
claims.source_text: If phosphate level is below 0.32 mmol/L, IV phosphate replacement should be considered as per local protocols … Calcium levels require close monitoring if IV phosphate is administered
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Start IV rehydration one hour before the insulin infusion. Do not give an insulin bolus.**
claims.source_text: IV rehydration should be commenced one hour prior to starting an insulin infusion … Do not use an insulin bolus at the initiation of therapy
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Make up:** 50 units clear/rapid-acting insulin in 49.5 mL 0.9% sodium chloride (1 unit/mL, syringe pump), or in 500 mL (0.1 unit/mL).
claims.source_text: Add 50 units of clear/rapid acting insulin (Actrapid HM or Humulin R or Novorapid) to 49.5 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride to form a 1 unit/mL solution via syringe pump or Add 50 units of clear/rapid acting insulin (Actrapid HM or Humulin R or Novorapid) to 500 mL 0.9% sodium chloride to form a 0.1 unit/mL solution
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Infusion rate: 0.1 units/kg/hour; consider 0.05 units/kg/hour** for inter-hospital transfer, children under 5, or BGL under 15 mmol/L at the start.
claims.source_text: An insulin infusion rate of 0.05 units/kg/hour should be considered for: Children undergoing inter-hospital transfer (limited access to biochemical monitoring) Children less than 5 years old Children with BGL <15 mmol/L at the time of commencement of the insulin infusion All other children with DKA should be commenced at a rate of 0.1 units/kg/hour
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Keep enough insulin running to clear ketones**; raise fluid glucose to 10% before cutting the insulin rate.
claims.source_text: Adequate insulin must be continued to clear ketones and correct acidosis … Aim to keep the blood glucose between 5-10 mmol/L by increasing the fluid glucose concentration to 10% before adjusting the insulin infusion rate
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Switch to subcutaneous insulin** when alert, eating and metabolically stable, ideally before a meal; **continue the infusion 30–60 minutes after the first subcutaneous rapid-acting dose.**
claims.source_text: Can be done when child is alert, eating and metabolically stable … Ideally just prior to a meal … Continue the insulin infusion for 30 to 60 minutes after the first subcutaneous injection of rapid-acting insulin, then cease
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mild DKA, with endocrine or paediatric input:** 0.1 units/kg Actrapid or Novorapid subcutaneously, then every 2 hours; every 4–6 hours once acidosis corrects.
claims.source_text: In children with mild DKA it may be appropriate to commence subcutaneous insulin in consultation with local endocrine or paediatric team … Commence 0.1 units/kg Actrapid or Novorapid subcutaneous injection, then 0.1 units/kg every 2 hours (or as directed by the treating endocrine team) … When acidosis has corrected change to Actrapid or Novorapid 0.1 units/kg every 4-6 hours
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Cerebral injury usually develops in the first 12 hours.** Early signs: headache, irritability, lethargy, vomiting worsening after therapy starts. Later: depressed consciousness, incontinence, thermal instability. Very late: bradycardia, raised BP, respiratory impairment.
claims.source_text: Clinically significant cerebral injury usually develops within the first 12 hours … Early: headache, irritability, lethargy, vomiting worsening after therapy initiated Later: depressed consciousness, incontinence, thermal instability Very late: bradycardia, increased BP, respiratory impairment
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Higher cerebral injury risk:** first presentation, long poor control, age under 5; severe hypocapnia, severe acidaemia, raised urea.
claims.source_text: Epidemiological risk factors First presentation diabetes Long history of poor control Age <5 years Biochemical risk factors at presentation Severe hypocapnia Severe acidaemia Increased urea
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Treat suspected cerebral injury:** consultant and ICU/retrieval, head up, **cut the fluid rate by one-third**, and give **mannitol 20% 0.5 g/kg IV over 20 minutes OR 3% sodium chloride 3 mL/kg IV over 15 minutes** — do not wait for imaging. No response in 15 minutes: discuss repeat doses with ICU.
claims.source_text: Discuss with consultant on call and liaise with intensive care or paediatric retrieval service to discuss transfer Nurse head up Reduce fluid infusion rate by one-third Give hyperosmolar therapy if clinically significant cerebral injury is apparent, do not wait for cerebral imaging Mannitol 20% (0.2 g/mL) dose: 0.5 g/kg IV over 20 minutes OR 3% sodium chloride 3 mL/kg IV over 15 minutes If no response within 15 minutes, discuss with intensive care specialist to consider repeated doses
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **BGL under 4.0 mmol/L: 10% glucose 2 mL/kg IV (repeat if needed) and switch fluids to 10% glucose. Do not stop the insulin infusion.** If it recurs despite 10% glucose in the preceding two hours, reduce insulin from 0.1 to 0.05 units/kg/hr (or from 0.05 to 0.03).
claims.source_text: A BGL <4.0 mmol/L should be treated with additional glucose as below 10% glucose IV bolus 2 mL/kg (repeat if required) and change rehydration fluids to include 10% glucose, with potassium chloride (maximum 60 mmol/L) as required Do not discontinue the insulin infusion If hypoglycaemia occurs despite use of 10% glucose in preceding two hours, decrease insulin infusion from 0.1 unit/kg/hr to 0.05 units/kg/hr (or to 0.03 units/kg/hr, if previously on 0.05 units/kg/hr)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Bicarbonate only for life-threatening hyperkalaemia or inotrope requirement**, after discussion with an intensivist.
claims.source_text: Only appropriate for children with life threatening hyperkalaemia or requiring inotropic support Discuss with intensive care specialist prior to administration
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the paediatric team for every child with DKA** and all newly diagnosed diabetes.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when All children with DKA All newly diagnosed diabetes mellitus
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Intensive care monitoring** for children under 2, coma, cardiovascular compromise, seizures, signs of cerebral oedema, or severe acidosis (pH under 7.1).
claims.source_text: Intensive care monitoring is recommended for Children <2 years of age Coma Cardiovascular compromise Seizures Signs of cerebral oedema Severe acidosis (pH <7.1
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetic ketoacidosis' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetic_ketoacidosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23
